key_insight: LLawCo teaches embodied multi-agent LLMs explicit cooperation "laws" learned from past failures so they align better with partners and task goals.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical training-and-reasoning recipe for building more reliable cooperative agents in decentralized, partially observable environments.
method: Reflect on failed interactions to extract misaligned behavioral patterns.
Derive high-level laws such as "Talk when necessary" and "Wait for partner."
Inject these laws into chain-of-thought reasoning via supervised fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates on PARTNR-Dialog and TDW-MAT, reporting average success-rate gains of 4.5% and 6.8% over state-of-the-art open-source communicative agent frameworks across four backbone LLMs.
watch_item: The approach depends on quality failure analysis and fine-tuning data, so learned laws may be task-specific and may not transfer cleanly to new environments or partner behaviors.
paper_title: LLawCo: Learning Laws of Cooperation for Modeling Embodied Multi-Agent Behavior
